alternate_names: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchal Nagar Sahib
festivals: Gurpurab (birth anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh Ji)

history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is one of the five Panj Takhts of SIKHISM. In 1708 Guru Gobind Singh Ji camped here after leaving for the Deccan; wounded by would-be assassins, he convalesced, declared the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru, named the town 'Abchalnagar' (Steadfast City), and merged with the Divine — his cremation spot (Angitha Sahib) lies within the sanctum. The present white-marble, golden-domed edifice was commissioned by Maharaja Ranjit Singh and built 1832–1837. The complex holds relics and shastars (weapons) of the Guru. The 300th anniversary of the Guruship of the Guru Granth Sahib was celebrated here in October 2008. State is MAHARASHTRA (CSV state column held town name).

name: Hazur Sahib Gurudwara
town_description: Nanded is a city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra on the banks of the Godavari River. One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities of the Deccan, it is the principal Sikh pilgrimage centre of southern India as the seat of Takht Hazur Sahib, and is connected by its own airport and a major railway junction.

travel.airport: Shri Guru Gobind Singh Ji Airport, Nanded (~10 km)
travel.railway: Hazur Sahib Nanded (NED) railway station (~2 km)
travel.road: Well connected by road to Hyderabad (~280 km), Aurangabad and the Marathwada region

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; Gurpurab and Baisakhi draw large congregations
